title: Weak or No A/C
summary: Mechanic-first diagnostic path for weak cooling, warm vents, compressor concerns, and refrigerant checks.
intro: Weak A/C should be separated into charge level, airflow, compressor operation, and control-command problems before compressor replacement is priced.
common_sounds: Warm air from vents with A/C on
Compressor clicks but does not stay engaged
A/C works while driving but fades at idle
Hissing, oily residue, or obvious leak evidence
quick_checks: Confirm blower airflow and cabin filter condition
Recover or measure refrigerant charge when required
Compare high and low side pressures to compressor command
Inspect condenser airflow and cooling fan operation
Check clutch, relay, pressure sensor, and control command before replacing the compressor

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Charge and Leak Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Low charge can imitate compressor failure, so prove charge and leak status first.
checks: Inspect oily residue at hoses, condenser, compressor, and service ports
Recover and recharge by weight when diagnosis requires it
Leak test before major parts are quoted

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Compressor and Airflow Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: When command and pressures prove compressor failure, include contamination and airflow checks in the estimate.
checks: Verify compressor command and clutch behavior
Check pressure response with A/C requested
Inspect condenser fan airflow at idle

recommended_repairs.title: A/C Compressor Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Use after charge, command, and pressure evidence confirms the compressor path.

recommended_repairs.title: Cooling Fan Diagnosis
recommended_repairs.description: Relevant when A/C cools poorly at idle because condenser airflow is weak.
